topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer development through mutation and clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce cancer through the selective growth of susceptible cells in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how that contribution is distinguished from chance and inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on activation and processing within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent tumour promotion for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogenesis and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility depends on the tissue and developmental context of exposure, then consolidate the preceding account of context-dependent carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how mutation patterns in cancer genomes can provide evidence of exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of carcinogenicity assessment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential can be assessed and why the available methods provide incomplete evidence about cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's main conclusions and frames their implications for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
